versions.title: Waterfront hearing draws 200, and a lot of opinions about parking
versions.body:
About 200 people came to Tuesday's public hearing on the Eastfield Waterfront rezoning. The council heard from 41 speakers in three hours.

Supporters talked about rents. Opponents talked about the Mill, the view and the ferry queue. Almost everyone talked about parking.

"I'm not against homes. I'm against my street becoming a car park," said one Eastfield resident.

The council votes on March 16.

versions.title: Letters: the Waterfront, the Mill and the 14 bus
versions.body:
"My daughter is 29 and lives with me because she cannot afford Eastfield. I'd like her to have the choice." — R. Patel, Eastfield

"Thirty percent below market is still more than a librarian earns. Ask one." — G. Moss, Old Town

"Before anyone builds 1,200 homes, could someone make the 14 bus run twice an hour?" — T. Kowalski, Northpoint

"The Mill was a workplace, not a monument. My grandfather lost two fingers there." — D. Ferris, the Heights

versions.title: Northgate posts record year on Northpoint sales
versions.body:
Northgate Development sold 212 homes in Northpoint this year, its best year since it was founded in 1998. The company says the Eastfield Waterfront would be "the biggest project in the city's history".

Chief executive Gerald Whitcombe said Northgate would "keep listening to Eastfield". Analysts say the project depends on the March rezoning vote.

versions.title: Northgate pays for new kits for Eastfield youth football
versions.body:
The Eastfield Under-12s will play in new kits this season, paid for by Northgate Development. The shirts carry the Northgate logo on the front and "Eastfield Strong" on the back.

"They look great and they were free," coach Lisa Moran said. "I'm not going to overthink it."

versions.title: Route 9 bike lane plan shelved again
versions.body:
A protected bike lane at the Route 9 and Harbor Street intersection has been pushed to next year's budget, for the third year running.

City staff say the lane would cost $1.4 million and require moving a bus stop. Cycling groups say the intersection has had 11 collisions since 2019.

versions.title: Mill workers' reunion fills the Legion hall
versions.body:
More than 300 former Calder Mill workers and their families filled the Legion hall on Saturday for the first reunion since the mill closed in 2009.

There were photos, a slideshow and a long argument about who ran the fastest forklift. "We were a family," said Bernice Doyle, 81, who worked in the weaving shed for 30 years.

versions.title: Iris Bell's dahlias take top prize at county fair
versions.body:
Iris Bell, 74, of Northpoint won best in show at the county fair for the third time with a dinner-plate dahlia she calls Harbour Sunset.

"The secret is patience and a lot of coffee grounds," she said. She has grown dahlias since 1971.

versions.title: Harbor Street agency named Newcomer of the Year
versions.body:
Brightline Media, a marketing agency with an office on Harbor Street, was named Newcomer of the Year at the Calder Business Awards on Thursday.

The judges praised its work for local businesses, including Harbor Dental and two restaurants on 4th Street. Brightline did not send anyone to collect the award.

versions.title: Five ways to make your small business sound local
versions.body:
1. Use the names of streets, not districts.

2. Post when your customers are awake.

3. Reply to every comment, even the grumpy ones.

4. Have a face. People trust faces.

5. Be consistent. Consistency is a form of respect.

versions.title: The Waterfront renderings have no shadows. Ask why.
versions.body:
Look at Northgate's pictures of the Eastfield Waterfront. Twelve towers, a sunny boardwalk, and not one shadow on the water.

Either the sun is directly overhead at all times in Eastfield, or someone does not want you to see what twelve towers do to the harbour at four in the afternoon.

versions.title: Reader tip: who is paying for the Waterfront mailers?
versions.body:
A reader in Eastfield has had four glossy Waterfront mailers this month, all from "Friends of Eastfield". There is no address on them and no website.

We looked. Friends of Eastfield is not registered anywhere we can find. If you know who they are, tell us.

Ordinance 26-031 rezones 14 acres of the former Calder Mill site from industrial to mixed residential.
Applicant: Northgate Development. Proposed: up to 1,200 homes, 30% below market rate for 15 years, a public boardwalk, a market hall.
Staff recommendation: approve with conditions (traffic study, ferry capacity, heritage plaque for the Mill).
Public comments received: 2,914.
New website is live! Book online, see our team, and finally find out where we park. Thank you @brightlinemedia for making it painless 🦷
New logo day! Designed by the lovely people at Brightline Media. Same bread, fancier bag 🥖
Went to the Waterfront open house. Free cookies, nice renderings, zero answers about the ferry queue. 3/10 would cookie again.
My kid has been on the Eastfield rental list for two years. I don't love towers. I love my kid more. Vote yes on the Waterfront.
Drove past the Mill this morning. Still weird without the sign. 23 years I walked under it.

versions.title: Harbor Street businesses count the cost of the flood
versions.body:
A week after the water main break, 26 of the 30 businesses between 2nd and 5th have reopened. Salty's Fish Bar will not reopen, and two shops say they are still waiting for their insurers.

The city has set up a $200,000 relief fund. Applications open on Monday.

versions.title: Library reopens children's corner with a reading marathon
versions.body:
The Eastfield library reopened its children's corner on Wednesday with a twelve-hour reading marathon. Staff read 64 books aloud, one of them twice by request.

"It's the best room in the building," said children's librarian Priya Shah.

versions.title: Northpoint ferry dock to reopen April 6
versions.body: The north ferry dock at Northpoint will reopen on April 6, a week later than planned, after both replaced pylons passed inspection. Ferries will return to the normal timetable the same day.

versions.title: Harbor Street: the same address, again
versions.body:
Two more buildings on Harbor Street have been sold since the flood. The buyer is registered at the same virtual office on Dock Road as the last three.

Still not saying what it means. Still the same address.
